summary: i-MESC is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in materials for energy storage and conversion, such as batteries and fuel cells. You study at Warsaw University of Technology, then Toulouse, then Amiens, Ljubljana or Bilbao, with the thesis possible at Drexel in the US or Deakin in Australia. Scholarships waive the €8,000 fee and pay €1,400 a month. Applications open on 9 November 2026 and close on 26 January 2027.
meta_title: i-MESC 2027: Erasmus Mundus energy storage master's scholarship
meta_description: i-MESC waives fees and pays €1,400 a month for a two-year master's in battery and energy materials across Warsaw, Toulouse and beyond. Apply by 26 January 2027.
covers: A full fee waiver. Self-funded students pay €4,000 a year.
€1,400 a month for 24 months, up to €33,600, for travel, visa and living costs.
Up to 80 Erasmus Mundus scholarships over four intakes, plus at least 40 industry scholarships of €20,000.
eligibility: Students from all over the world.

A bachelor's of at least 180 ECTS in chemistry, physics, chemical engineering, materials science, materials process engineering or electrochemistry modelling. Other backgrounds are considered if compatible. Final-year students must graduate before 1 June.
English: a certificate from your university that your studies were taught in English, or IELTS 6.5, TOEFL 87, Cambridge B2 First or a CEFR B2 certificate. Other tests are not accepted.
how_to_apply: Apply online from 9 November 2026 at 14:00 to 26 January 2027 at 12:00, Paris time.

Upload your passport, certified transcripts translated into English by a sworn translator, a Europass CV of up to two pages, two recommendation letters on the programme's template, your English certificate and a video of up to two minutes.
Results come as main, reserve and non-selected lists.
watch_out: The programme calls its dates indicative, and one of its pages misprints the closing year as 2026. Apply well before 26 January 2027.
A medium-of-instruction letter from a Ghanaian or Nigerian university meets the English requirement.
Students without a scholarship get €2,300 towards mobility and visas.
documents: Certified transcripts with sworn English translations
Two recommendation letters on the template
